judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward definitional passage identifying the customer, the CAB and the named lender; no term in it carries competing meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fixes 'the lender' as DSI Lending Resources, while Arbitration Paragraph 1 (c017) defines 'the Lender' open-endedly as 'any Lender who provides you with a loan as a result of our services', a small mismatch that could matter to who may enforce the arbitration clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The services are described only as things the CAB 'will attempt to' do, with soft boundaries ('where available', 'upon request', 'may be provided throughout the term'), so what performance is actually owed for the fee is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against COST AND PAYMENT TERMS (c004), which charges a 708.90% annualized fee for services whose content this clause leaves largely optional, but the two can be read together without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two lines asserting the fee 'is not interest' yet must be included in the finance charge; the characterisation is conclusory but the sentence itself has one meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with c004, which folds the CAB fee into the Finance Charge and a 713.38% APR, and with c005's 10% per annum charge — a characterisation tension rather than a textual conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arithmetic does not close: $3.00 interest plus a $556.15 CAB fee is not the stated $561.15 Finance Charge, and the 'Total of Payments is $86.15' plainly contradicts ten bi-weekly payments of $86.15, a mechanical error that changes what the customer owes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The stated 10.00% lender interest matches c002 and c005, but the numbers here cannot be reconciled with the payment schedule they themselves recite, and the refund-on-prepayment sentence sits against the acceleration language in DEFAULT (c007).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It enumerates reimbursement items and closes with unqualified 'attorneys' fees, and costs of collection', an open-ended catch-all whose reach against the enumerated fees is not fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Collection Expenses (c012) limits the same exposure to 'reasonable attorneys' fees', so the unqualified fee entitlement here is in mild tension with that later provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is scrambled and incomplete — 'Chapter $ of the Texas Business and Commerce Code' names no chapter and the opening clause is transposed — and the LOC cap 'principal, interest, returned item fee, and late fee, as applicable' leaves the ceiling uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its automatic-revocation-on-cancellation sentence depends on the cancellation right in c033/c034, whose three-day trigger is itself stated two different ways, but nothing here squarely contradicts another operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is textually damaged in its trigger list and ends with the open catch-all 'any other right or remedy allowed by law and this Agreement' sitting beside one enumerated remedy, the classic general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Default (3) makes failure to perform obligations owed to the Lender a default under this Agreement, which reaches outside the instrument, though NOTICES AND WAIVERS (c008) waives the notices that would otherwise attend the acceleration this clause imposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long list of waivers, each specific and individually definite; 'others responsible' is undefined but the operative content is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The statements that 'we are not required to file suit or arbitrate' and 'we may sue or arbitrate with one or more persons' sit awkwardly beside Arbitration Paragraphs 3 and 4 (c021, c022), which make arbitration the exclusive individual route once elected.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence is convoluted and refers to a 'Jury Trial Waiver and Arbitration Agreement' that one may 'reject', terminology found nowhere else in the document, leaving its operation obscure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The heading of the arbitration section is 'WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL AND ARBITRATION PROVISION' with a ninety-day OPT-OUT (c027), not a 'rejection', so the cross-reference does not cleanly map onto the instrument's own scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard usury-savings boilerplate; every sentence has a single meaning even if 'amortizing, prorating, allocating and spreading' is technical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The identical text is repeated verbatim in the LOC clause (c006) and inside Arbitration Paragraph 4 (c022); duplication is untidy but creates no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prior to initiating any claim' plus 'a reasonable opportunity of not less than 60 days to cure' leaves it unclear whether this is a mandatory condition precedent and to what proceedings it attaches, and 'any corrective action shall relieve us ... of any liability' is drafted wholly one-sidedly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps and competes with the 30-day remedy notice in Arbitration Paragraph 4 (c022) and with the preserved small-claims right in Paragraph 6 (c024); the 'cumulative' saving sentence tries to harmonise them but does not resolve which period governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable attorneys' fees ... and all costs and disbursements' is broad but conventional; the second sentence is a statutory admonition awkwardly dropped into a fee clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'reasonable' qualifier here narrows the unqualified attorneys' fee entitlement in c005, a difference a court could be asked to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence of stipulation with no operative ambiguity; 'for all purposes' is broad but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is fully consistent with Arbitration Paragraph 7 (c025), which invokes the FAA on the same interstate-commerce footing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deliberately asymmetric — unlimited transfer by the CAB, none by the customer — and it speaks only of rights, titles and interests, saying nothing about delegation of the CAB's duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Arbitration Paragraph 8 (c026) extends the arbitration clause to 'successors and assigns' and related third parties, so the assignment power interacts with who may compel arbitration, but no contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely factual address and contact details with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The address matches those given in the pre-suit notice clause (c011), the opt-out clause (c027) and the cancellation notices (c036).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is explanatory preamble rather than operative text, and its generalities ('Pre-arbitration discovery may be limited', 'A court rarely overturns an arbitrator's decision') set no enforceable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tells the customer that arbitrating parties 'waive their rights to file a lawsuit and proceed in court', which is flatly qualified by Paragraph 6's preserved small-claims forum (c024) and by Paragraph 3's fallback to court (c021) — a recital-versus-operative mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It gives 'dispute' the 'broadest possible meaning' and then, in (a), sweeps in 'the validity and scope of this Arbitration Provision' — a delegation of arbitrability that is one of the most frequently construed phrases in consumer contracts, and (b) refers to 'this Disclosure Statement', a document this Agreement never defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph (a) commits validity questions to the arbitrator while Paragraph 3 (c021) reserves the validity of the class waiver 'solely' to a court, and Paragraph 6 (c024) carves out small-claims disputes entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short capitalised acknowledgment of jury-trial waiver whose meaning is plain despite OCR damage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It extends the waiver to 'the Lender and/or our/its related third parties', non-signatories whose ability to invoke the clause depends on Paragraph 8 (c026), but the two point the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Single-sentence acknowledgment with an express small-claims carve-out; nothing in the wording admits of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Paragraph 6 (c024) exactly on the small-claims exception, though it is broader than the introduction (c016), which describes an unqualified waiver of court.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver of representative and class participation is stated in flat, capitalised terms, and 'in any other representative capacity' is a catch-all after specifics but its reach is reasonably clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its absolute terms are qualified by Paragraph 3 (c021), which contemplates the dispute proceeding in court if the class waiver is not enforced, and by Paragraph 8 (c026), which voids the whole provision in that event.
